artist.name: Clara Mae
artist.place_of_origin: Gävle area, Sweden (raised / studied; exact birthplace not verified)
artist.short_description: Swedish songwriter whose intimate breakup narratives move between bright Scandinavian pop and country-tinged reflection.
artist.biography: Clara Mae is a Swedish singer-songwriter associated with Gävle, where she studied jazz singing and piano before pursuing music professionally in Stockholm. She developed her craft writing for other performers, with credits connected to dance-pop artists including David Guetta and Tiësto. Her collaboration with Norwegian electronic duo KREAM brought her voice to the 2016 track ‘Taped Up Heart,’ an early international breakthrough. She subsequently signed with Big Beat Records and established a solo identity built around candid relationship stories. Her 2018 six-song project ‘Sorry for Writing All the Songs About You,’ co-written with Cassandra Ströberg, follows the emotional arc of a romance, from early excitement to separation and acceptance. In a contemporary interview, Clara Mae explained that writing the songs helped her work through experiences from past relationships. Her 2020 collection ‘Drunk On Emotions’ continued that emotional focus and featured collaborations with gnash and country singer Russell Dickerson. The standalone 2021 single ‘Not Sad Anymore’ offered a different perspective: rediscovering independence after heartbreak. On the 2026 album ‘My Roots,’ her music moved toward a softer, more organic palette with country influences. Across those chapters, Clara Mae has emphasized story-led songwriting, melodic accessibility, and emotional specificity. For Afterglow listeners, her catalogue offers a bridge between polished Scandinavian pop, reflective breakup songs, and country-tinged singer-songwriter music.
